injuries.longComment: Padover added that the team hopes to provide an update on Jones after the break. Madina Okot will likely continue to see a slight bump in minutes behind Angel Reese until Jones is cleared to play.
injuries.shortComment: General manager Dan Padover said Friday that Jones (leg) won't return to game action before the FIBA World Cup break, Meghan L. Hall of USA Today reports.

injuries.longComment: She will now "focus on recovering an aggravated right knee injury." She hadn't played since July 3 and her rehab didn't progress as quickly as she would've hoped. She appeared in 19 games and posted averages of 14.2 points, 3.2 rebounds and 4.9 assists.
injuries.shortComment: Diggins (knee) will miss the remainder of the 2026 WNBA season, Sara Jane Gamelli of BallisLife.com reports.

injuries.longComment: With the WNBA about to go on a hiatus for the World Cup, the Sky are taking a cautious approach with Carrington for Saturday. Her absence opens the door for Gabriela Jaquez to take on a bigger workload.
injuries.shortComment: Carirngton (foot) is out for Saturday's game against the Liberty.

injuries.longComment: The season-ending knee injury is a devastating development for Jackson and the Sky, as the 25-year-old forward was well on her way to a career-best campaign. Through Chicago's first four games, Jackson averaged 18.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.5 three-pointers in 29.5 minutes per contest. After Jackson's early exit in Sunday's contest, Aicha Coulibaly opened the second half with the starters and looks to be the most likely candidate to move into the top unit for the Sky's next game Wednesday versus the Wings.
injuries.shortComment: The Sky announced Tuesday that Jackson will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a torn ACL in her left knee during Sunday's 86-79 win over the Lynx.

injuries.longComment: Marshall will be inactive as Connecticut manages her eligibility as a developmental player. Her next chance to suit up will come Sept. 17 against Atlanta.
injuries.shortComment: Marshall (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Dallas.

injuries.longComment: Nelson-Ododa will miss a fourth consecutive game due to a right knee injury. In her absence, Raegan Beers could remain in the starting five. Nelson-Ododa will have an extended period to recover, with her next chance to suit up coming Sept. 17 against Atlanta.
injuries.shortComment: Nelson-Ododa (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Dallas.

injuries.longComment: Griner will miss an eighth straight game due to a left knee injury, and her next opportunity to suit up won't come until Sept. 17 against the Dream. If Olivia Nelson-Ododa (knee) joins Griner on the inactive list, Raegan Beers and Nell Angloma would be candidates for increased playing time.
injuries.shortComment: Griner (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Wings.

injuries.longComment: Burke is headed to Germany to represent Turkey in the 2026 FIBA World Cup. She should report back to the WNBA club for the Sep. 17 matchup against the Dream.
injuries.shortComment: Connecticut announced Thursday that Burke will miss the Sun's next two games.

injuries.longComment: Lacan will report to Team France early after averaging 11.6 points, 4.6 assists, 1.9 rebounds and 1.7 steals across 28.4 minutes per game in her first 27 regular-season appearances this year. Charlisse Leger-Walker, Saniya Rivers and Hailey Van Lith could all see increased playing time in Lacan's stead.
injuries.shortComment: The Sun announced Sunday that Lacan will join Team France for the FIBA World Cup and miss the Sun's next four games.

injuries.longComment: Fudd has been sidelined since early August due to her ongoing right knee soreness, and she'll undergo a procedure that will ultimately end her rookie season. Across 30 regular-season appearances (24 starts) this year, she averaged 13.1 points, 1.8 assists, 1.7 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 31.7 minutes per game. In her absence, Odyssey Sims, Alanna Smith and Alysha Clark have seen increased roles, and that trend will likely continue down the stretch as the Wings compete for a playoff berth.
injuries.shortComment: Fudd will undergo an arthroscopic procedure to address her right knee soreness and will be sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 season.

injuries.longComment: Verona is signed to a developmental contract, so she has only appeared in one regular-season game for Dallas during the 2026 campaign. She will now head overseas, where she will suit up for the Italian National Team for the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup. It's unknown whether Verona will be back with the Wings, though her departure will allow the team to sign another player to a developmental deal.
injuries.shortComment: Verona's contract was temporarily suspended by the Wings Saturday.

injuries.longComment: out
injuries.shortComment: out

injuries.longComment: Salaun struggled to find the bottom of the net in this one, though she managed to contribute elsewhere by turning in her best rebounding night since July 10. She'll end her streak of double-digit scoring performances at five games following Thursday's showing. Salaun will now set her sights on the FIBA World Cup and is slated to miss Sunday's matchup against the Fire to head overseas. She's expected to return to the Valkyries in time for a Sept. 18 matchup against the Fire.
injuries.shortComment: Salaun registered seven points (3-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and seven rebounds in 24 minutes during Thursday's 79-60 win over New York.

injuries.longComment: Williams did the majority of her scoring from beyond the arc and drilled four triples for the fifth time this season, a mark that currently stands as a season high for the 29-year-old. Following Thursday's victory, she'll head overseas for the FIBA World Cup and be away from the team for Sunday's matchup against the Fire, likely opening up more playing time for Laeticia Amihere, Tiffany Hayes and Kaila Charles. Williams is expected to rejoin Golden State prior to the Valkyries' Sept. 18 matchup against Portland.
injuries.shortComment: Williams recorded 16 points (6-15 FG, 4-8 3Pt), four rebounds, three assists and two steals in 23 minutes during Thursday's 79-60 win over the Liberty.

injuries.longComment: Rupert signed a multi-year contract with Golden State during the offseason and missed the start of training camp due to an overseas commitment. Her status for the 2026 regular season now appears to be in jeopardy due to her pregnancy. The 24-year-old made 21 regular-season appearances (11 starts) for the Valkyries last year and averaged 9.3 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 23.1 minutes per game. If Rupert is sidelined in 2026, Janelle Salaun, Kiah Stokes and Laeticia Amihere are candidates to see increased work.
injuries.shortComment: Rupert is pregnant, and the Valkyries have filed for a replacement contract ahead of the 2026 season, Alexa Philippou of ESPN.com reports Thursday.

injuries.longComment: Latson will sit out Las Vegas' final game before the FIBA World Cup break. Her next chance to play will come against the Storm on Sept. 17.
injuries.shortComment: Latson (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Tempo.

injuries.longComment: It's a big blow for the defending-champion Aces ahead of the postseason. Smith started all 38 of her appearances for Las Vegas, so a spot in the first unit is now open. Brianna Turner appears to the most likely candidate to replace Smith in the starting lineup going forward.
injuries.shortComment: The Aces announced Thursday that Smith will be sidelined for the rest of the season after suffering a non-contact left leg injury during Sunday's game versus the Tempo, per Chelsea Leite of TSN.

injuries.longComment: Nye is not currently with the team. Her next chance to play will come Thursday, Sept. 17, in Dallas.
injuries.shortComment: Nye (not with team) will miss Sunday's game in Seattle.

injuries.longComment: Buenavida has yet to make her WNBA debut and will remain on the inactive list Sunday. Her next opportunity to play will come against the Liberty on Sept. 18.
injuries.shortComment: Buenavida (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dream.

injuries.longComment: This is an expected move ahead of the World Cup. Delaere has just been an emergency depth piece for the Lynx this season.
injuries.shortComment: The Lynx temporarily suspended Delaere's contract Tuesday.

injuries.longComment: This is related to the upcoming World Cup. Additionally, the Lynx suspended Antonia Delaere's contract. The Team could lean more on Anastasiia Kosu in the meantime.
injuries.shortComment: The Lynx temporarily suspended Juhasz's contract Tuesday.

injuries.longComment: out
injuries.shortComment: out

injuries.longComment: Plum is still not feeling the effects of a lingering lower leg injury and will be shut down with the Mercury out of the playoffs. The star guard is set to become a free agent at the conclusion of the season. In five appearances with the Mercury, she averaged 15.8 points and 2.8 assists.
injuries.shortComment: Plum (leg) will miss the remainder of the 2026 WNBA season, Alexa Philippou of ESPN.com reports.

injuries.longComment: Copper was expected to suit up for this contest, but in the end, the star guard won't be available, meaning Phoenix will be without one of their more reliable scoring options. Copper is averaging a career-high 21.3 points along with 3.6 rebounds and 1.9 assists over 32.9 minutes per contest this season. Alexa Held will start in her absence.
injuries.shortComment: Copper (ankle) is out for Saturday's game against Toronto, Jenna Ortiz of The Arizona Republic reports.

injuries.longComment: out
injuries.shortComment: out

injuries.longComment: Linskens is preparing to represent Belgium in the upcoming FIBA World Cup. She'll likely report back to Phoenix ahead of the Sep. 17 matchup in Portland.
injuries.shortComment: The Mercury temporarily suspended Linskens' contract Wednesday.

injuries.longComment: Nogic had her contract temporarily suspended June 20 and will now be out for the remainder of the WNBA season, as she's slated to compete overseas in Russia with an eye on leading the Serbian national team in the EuroBasket 2027 qualifiers. The guard appeared in 16 games (seven starts) for Phoenix, averaging 10.4 points, 1.6 assists and 1.1 rebounds in 20.2 minutes per contest. With Nogic out of the fold for the foreseeable future, Alexa Held stands to continue benefiting from expanded opportunities in the backcourt.
injuries.shortComment: Nogic (not injury related) intends to play professionally in Russia and won't return to Phoenix this season, Aya Abdeen of TheIXSports.com reports.

injuries.longComment: Leite will represent France in the FIBA World Cup, and she'll miss the Fire's game against Golden State on Sunday at the very least. With the second-year floor general unavailable, Holly Winterburn, Jordan Harrison and Teja Oblak are candidates for increased playing time.
injuries.shortComment: The Fire temporarily suspended Leite's contract Saturday.

injuries.longComment: Buhner will represent Germany in the 2026 FIBA World Cup. She will presumably return to the Fire for the Sep. 17 meeting with the Mercury, though that's not guaranteed.
injuries.shortComment: The Fire temporarily suspended Buhner's contract Wednesday.

injuries.longComment: Geiselsoder will represent Germany at the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup, and since she's been out of the rotation for a while, she's leaving early for preparation and won't return this season. She ends the season with averages of 4.5 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.3 assists across 16.6 minutes per game in 21 appearances (nine starts).
injuries.shortComment: Geiselsoder (personal) won't return this season, according to Sean Highkin of RoseGardenReport.com.

injuries.longComment: Barker was helped to the locker room in the first quarter of Wednesday's loss to the Wings, and she's now been diagnosed with a season-ending injury. The second-year guard took on a significant role for the Fire after the club selected her in the 2026 WNBA Expansion Draft. Across 26 regular-season games (15 starts), the 24-year-old averaged 10.7 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 0.9 steals in 24.7 minutes per contest. Karlie Samuelson, Teja Oblak and Nyadiew Puoch are candidates for increased playing time in Barker's stead.
injuries.shortComment: The Fire announced Friday that Barker will undergo surgery to repair a torn ACL and will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

injuries.longComment: Feagin agreed to a developmental contract with Portland on June 24 after spending time in Los Angeles. After appearing in 16 regular-season games for the Sparks in 2025, the 23-year-old played in only three regular-season contests in 2026, logging a combined 10 minutes. Feagin had yet to make her debut with the Fire, though that will now need to wait, assuming Portland keeps her on the roster moving ahead.
injuries.shortComment: Feagin (knee) was diagnosed with a torn left ACL on Thursday and will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign, WNBA reporter Kareem Copeland reports.

injuries.longComment: This will be Hiedeman's fourth consecutive game on the inactive list, and it's not a great sign that she continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff. For now, she should be considered questionable for Seattle's next game against Las Vegas on Sept. 17.
injuries.shortComment: Hiedeman (shoulder) won't play Sunday against the Sparks.

injuries.longComment: Fam is heading to Germany for World Cup play. She should rejoin the Storm for the Sep. 17 game against the Aces.
injuries.shortComment: Fam had her contract temporarily suspended Thursday.

injuries.longComment: Sabally is sidelined by a calf injury anyways and is scheduled to be re-evaluated in a few weeks. A return on Sept. 18 could potentially be on the table.
injuries.shortComment: The Tempo suspended Sabally's (calf) contract on Thursday.

injuries.longComment: This is an expected move ahead of the World Cup. With Conde away from the team, the Tempo will likely lean more on Laura Juskaite and Isabelle Harrison in the short term.
injuries.shortComment: The Tempo temporarily suspended Conde's contract on Thursday.

injuries.longComment: Allemand is representing Belgium for the upcoming FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, so she's in line to miss at least Toronto's next three contests. With the Tempo missing several key players, Teonni Key should experience a considerable boost in short-term fantasy appeal.
injuries.shortComment: The Tempo temporarily suspended the contract of Allemand (head) on Tuesday.

injuries.longComment: It sounds like Mabrey's status is in doubt for the remainder of the year, as the Tempo are already eliminated from playoff contention. Toronto will be out of action until Sep. 18 following its next three contests while the WNBA accommodates the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup. Kia Nurse and Isabelle Harrison should continue to help pick up the slack going forward.
injuries.shortComment: Head coach Sandy Brondello announced Sunday that Mabrey (adductor) will be re-evaluated in a few weeks.

injuries.longComment: Brittney Sykes (foot) will also miss the final eight games for Toronto. According to coach Sandy Brondello, Morrow is not facing a lengthy recovery. Kia Nurse and Ornella Bankole are candidates to step into larger roles the rest of the way.
injuries.shortComment: Morrow (knee) will miss the rest of the 2026 season, Chelsea Leite of TSN reports.

injuries.longComment: This is a tough blow for Toronto, but Sykes' foot issues have continued to linger. She will finish the campaign with averages of 18.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.2 steals and 0.5 blocks in 29.4 minutes per contest. Kia Nurse and Ornella Bankole could see larger roles the rest of the way with this news.
injuries.shortComment: Sykes (foot) will miss the remainder of the 2026 season, Chelsea Leite of TSN reports.
